author: Nayan Seth,Lucy Quaggin
description:
More than one-third of Americans see China, and not the United States, as the global leader in artificial intelligence (AI), according to a Pew Research Centre survey released on Thursday, as US President Donald Trump confirmed the technology would be on the agenda when his Chinese counterpart visits the US later this year.
The survey found that 36 per cent of Americans believe China is more advanced than the United States in developing artificial intelligence. By comparison, only 12 per cent...
title: More Americans think China is world leader in AI, new survey reveals

author: Albee Zhang
description:
There is a change in the skies and waters around Taiwan.
In the first half of this year, the number of People’s Liberation Army (PLA) fighter jets detected near the island more than halved year on year to 1,334.
It was a three-year low and marked the lowest operational tempo since 2023, according to a tally by the South China Morning Post based on data from Taiwan’s defence ministry.
At the same time, the number of days no PLA jets were detected by Taiwan hit a new high, and the PLA did not...
title: Why PLA fighter jet sorties near Taiwan dropped to a 3-year low in the first half of 2026

author: Han Li
description:
US senators broadly agree that Chinese connected vehicles should be kept off American roads. But a bipartisan attempt to codify and expand existing restrictions has exposed divisions over whether the proposed ban could ensnare European carmakers and increase costs for American electric-vehicle producers.
The Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation advanced the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, a bill that would prohibit the import, manufacture and sale of connected...
title: US senators clash over scope of Chinese connected-vehicle ban

author: Nayan Seth,Mark Magnier
description:
The United States imposed late on Thursday a fresh wave of tariffs against 60 countries, including China, Japan, South Korea, India and European Union member states, hours before a temporary 10 per cent blanket levy was due to expire.
The tariffs, ranging from 10 to 12.5 per cent, are the outcome of a Section 301 investigation into forced labour, with Washington arguing that existing measures have failed to keep goods produced with forced labour out of supply chains.
“Today’s action will begin...
title: US slaps fresh tariffs on China, 50-plus countries in latest wave

author: Wenran Jiang
description:
Mid-July should have been a moment of quiet satisfaction in Beijing. Fresh data showed China’s favourability surpassing that of the United States in 25 of 37 nations surveyed by Pew Research Centre, including key European countries. Domestically, the second-quarter gross domestic product growth of 4.3 per cent, while softer than the first financial quarter, kept the annual target within reach.
The logic was simple: with the US distracted by Donald Trump’s erratic trade wars and isolationist...
title: As the West finds common cause, China prepares for the worst

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Brazil that Beijing would continue to support its sovereignty, security, and development interests hours after a 25 per cent US tariff on Brazilian goods took effect.
Wang met Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira on Wednesday in Manila, on the sidelines of the 59th meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) foreign ministers, where Vieira is also attending the third Brazil-Asean ministerial.
China would go on to “support Brazil in...
title: China vows to defend Brazil’s sovereignty as Trump’s 25% tariff bites

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The Pentagon has added Fudan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University to a list of foreign institutions deemed a threat to US national security, extending Washington’s research-security crackdown to two of China’s most prestigious civilian universities.
The updated list identifies 88 institutions in mainland China and bars US Department of Defence-funded researchers from collaborating with them, or using their equipment, under restrictions taking effect in the 2026 financial year.
The...
title: Pentagon expands blacklist to include China’s top civilian universities

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The EU has watered down its latest round of sanctions on Moscow after concluding that banning Greek companies from transporting Russian gas to third countries could hand strategically important shipping assets to China.
To remove a Greek veto against the 21st package of measures aimed at hobbling Russia’s war machine, the bloc’s member states agreed to allow EU operators to continue transporting Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) to third countries for one year.
Officials explained that China’s...
title: EU waters down Russia sanctions over fears China could seize key LNG assets

author: Mark Magnier
description:
At Zion Foodtrucks in the US state of Colorado, American-made steel and aluminium are combined with globally sourced stoves, refrigerators, vents and titanium piping to transform everyday vehicles into mobile restaurants.
But instead of benefiting from President Donald Trump’s push to revive US manufacturing, the company says it has been squeezed by higher costs and tougher competition.
Since taking office, Trump’s import taxes on steel and aluminium have hit 50 per cent tied to his “beautiful”...
title: Trump’s manufacturing push meets reality as costs rise and investment stalls

author: Fan Chen
description:
Scientific ties can be a stabilising force in relations between China and the US but as the two countries jostle for a hi-tech edge, maintaining these links will mean going beyond simple competition versus cooperation.
To get there, Beijing and Washington will need to keep in continuous contact and have clearly defined boundaries, with narrower areas of collaboration.
That was the finding Zhao Minghao, a professor at Fudan University’s Institute of International Studies, and Chen Yutong, a...
title: Can science bridge the US-China trust gap? Maybe with new rules, researchers say

author: Zhang Tong
description:
For the first time, China has produced Fields Medal winners educated on its own soil – and two at once.
Chinese mathematicians Wang Hong and Deng Yu took the honour, alongside John Pardon and Jacob Tsimerman.
The Fields Medal is the top honour for young mathematicians under 40 years of age. The medals, along with a modest cash prize, were given out on Thursday at the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) in Philadelphia.
The prestigious medal, often called the “Nobel Prize of...
title: Fields Medal win: Wang Hong, Deng Yu are first Chinese nationals to score top maths honour

author: Fan Chen,Khushboo Razdan,Alyssa Chen
description:
China and the United States’ agreement to pursue stability appeared to be holding, analysts said, even as President Donald Trump seemed determined to rock the boat ahead of the leaders’ second summit of the year in September.
The assessment came as Beijing issued a measured response to his allegations of Chinese interference in the 2020 US elections.
That restraint and recent tangible gestures – including Washington lifting sanctions on Hong Kong and the expected trip to the US this week by a...
title: Why Trump’s claim that Beijing meddled in US election hasn’t put ties on ice

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The People’s Liberation Army has showcased new airburst munitions that shower targets with metal fragments, offering the latest hint of how its long-range rocket artillery might be used in a Taiwan conflict.
Released on Sunday by the PLA-affiliated China Military Bugle social media channel under the title “Steel Rain”, the footage shows several PHL-191-launched rockets detonating above what appears to be a desert training range, showering a wide area with high-speed metal fragments.
The video...
title: What do the PLA’s ‘Steel Rain’ shells say about its war plans for Taiwan?

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
Southern and eastern China are bracing for another round of severe weather after twin typhoons and widespread flooding this month.
China’s top flood control and drought relief body held an emergency inter-agency meeting on Wednesday to coordinate disaster prevention ahead of the expected 12th named storm of the season.
Meanwhile, rainfall remains widespread and intense nationwide, including regions still recovering from recent storms. Rivers and lakes are still swollen in some areas and the soil...
title: China braces for up to 3 typhoons in devastating wake of Bavi, Maysak

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
The foreign ministers of China and the United States adopted a largely cordial tone following a meeting on Wednesday where they discussed Chinese President Xi Jinping’s upcoming trip to the US rather than President Donald Trump’s accusations of election interference by Beijing.
Their talks were “pragmatic, positive and constructive”, China’s Wang Yi said in a statement after the conversation in Manila. Marco Rubio of the US said that “great difference” between the two countries must be managed...
title: China, US emphasise stability amid lingering tensions

author: Shi Huang
description:
How many electrons does it take to store a single bit of information?
For today’s most advanced dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips from Samsung and SK Hynix, the answer is roughly 200,000.
That is the price of reliability – a vast reservoir of charge needed to ensure a “1” or “0” does not fade into noise.
But a team at Fudan University in Shanghai has just collapsed that number to its theoretical floor: one.
In a paper published on July 16 in Science, microelectronics professor Zhou Peng...
title: China’s new chip stores data with a single electron, breaking AI memory bottleneck

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Mainland China is conducting two-day live-fire exercises in the Taiwan Strait off coastal waters of the southeastern province of Fujian, its maritime authority said.
The drill will run from 6am to 6pm on both Thursday and Friday, according to a navigation warning issued by the China Maritime Safety Administration on Wednesday.
People’s Liberation Army drills usually peak in mid and late July as the PLA seeks to improve its capacities in harsh environments, including under extreme heat.


Based...
title: PLA conducts 2 days of live-fire drills in Taiwan Strait off Fujian island

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is facing mounting domestic backlash over a potential trade deal with the United States that would place India at the centre of US President Donald Trump’s efforts to redirect agricultural exports displaced by the US-China trade conflict, raising fresh questions about New Delhi’s broader strategic alignment with Washington against Beijing.
Thousands of farmers from the northern state of Punjab marched towards Delhi on Tuesday to oppose what they described as a...
title: US-China trade war reaches India’s streets as Modi weighs risks of Washington bet

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
In the past week, one regulation has forced many people in China to say goodbye to long-standing “relationships”. As of July 15, the government placed artificial intelligence (AI) companions under tight supervision. It comes as automated companions have experienced something of a boom over the past few years.
According to the rules, AI-human interactions should not encourage violence or harm users’ physical and psychological well-being. Moreover, AI bots should not lure users into sharing...
title: China’s crackdown on AI companions won’t fill the emotional void

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday warned his Philippine counterpart that Manila would “bear the bitter consequences” if it tried to provoke Beijing with the help of other countries.
Wang made the remark as he lodged a “strong protest” during talks with Theresa Lazaro, the Philippines’ top diplomat, in Manila over what he called an “aggressive act of ramming a Chinese law enforcement vessel” at a disputed reef in the South China Sea on Monday.
It was the third day Beijing has...
title: After latest clash at sea, China warns Philippines of ‘bitter consequences’

author: Ling Xin
description:
China has brought online a record-breaking particle accelerator that can produce the world’s most intense beams of charged atoms.
It gives scientists a new tool to create previously unknown atomic nuclei and advance research on cancer treatment and spacecraft materials.
Scientific operations have now begun at the 2.6 billion yuan (US$384.1 million) facility in Huizhou, Guangdong province after construction was completed on Tuesday, state news agency Xinhua reported.
Known as the High Intensity...
title: China fires up powerful particle accelerator to unlock secrets of atoms
